citation_bindings.exact_text: For unresectable, locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC) and limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), the current standard of care is platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) followed by consolidation immune-checkpoint blockade, a sequence that significantly prolongs progression-free and overall survival.

Circulating tumor DNA, metabolic imaging parameters, and real-time immune-profiling are being integrated into non-invasive biomarker platforms that track response and guide post-concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) immunotherapy decisions.

This review mainly synthesizes clinical evidence on the efficacy of ICI, currently the most widely used immunotherapy, in LC patients concomitant with COPD and elucidates potential immunological and molecular mechanisms underlying observed clinical benefits, including heightened programmed cell death protein ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, elevated tumor mutational burden, increased human leukocyte antigen I (HLA-I) expression, enriched tissue-resident memory T cells and mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and a macrophage polarization shift toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, with benefits appearing largely attributable to patients with mild-to-moderate airflow obstruction.
